recipes.name: Prik Gaeng Kiew Wan (Green Curry Paste)
recipes.flavorProfile: Bright, grassy and fiercely hot, with lemongrass, galangal and lime peel over a salty shrimp paste base.
recipes.healthBenefit: A spoonful carries fresh chilies, garlic, shallot and aromatic roots, though it is salty and used in small amounts.

ingredients.cutPrep: long green chilies, seeded and chopped

ingredients.prepNote: in place of coriander root, which the database does not hold; leaves count for the root

instructions: Toast the coriander and cumin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until fragrant and a shade darker, then grind them fine with the peppercorns.
Pound the salt and chilies in a heavy mortar for 3 to 5 minutes, until they break down into a coarse mash.
Add the lemongrass, galangal, lime peel and coriander root a little at a time, pounding 5 to 8 minutes, until fibrous pieces are gone.
Add the shallot and garlic and pound 3 to 5 minutes more, then work in the shrimp paste and ground spices until the paste is smooth and even.
Pack into a clean jar, press plastic onto the surface and keep refrigerated for up to 1 week, or freeze in tablespoon portions for up to 3 months.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the salt and shrimp paste, so a little goes a long way.

recipes.name: Prik Gaeng Phed (Red Curry Paste)
recipes.flavorProfile: Deep brick red, warm and smoky from dried chilies, with lemongrass and galangal behind a savoury shrimp paste finish.
recipes.healthBenefit: Dried chilies, garlic and shallot bring flavour without fat, though the paste is salty and meant for small amounts.

ingredients.prepNote: 7 to 8 long and 3 to 4 small dried chilies
1 tbsp at 5 g per tbsp; in place of coriander root, which the database does not hold; leaves count for the root

instructions: Toast the coriander seeds, cumin and peppercorns in a dry pan until lightly browned, then grind them to a fine powder in a mortar.
Add the chilies and salt and grind until fine.
Add the lemongrass, galangal and coriander root and pound until the fibres break apart.
Work in the shallots, then the garlic, until no pieces remain, then the lime peel.
Mash in the shrimp paste until fully combined. Keep refrigerated up to 1 week, or freeze in tablespoon portions for several months.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the carotenoids in the dried red chilies.
From the salt and shrimp paste.

recipes.name: Prik Gaeng Kari (Yellow Curry Paste)
recipes.flavorProfile: Mild, golden and warmly spiced, with fresh and ground turmeric, cumin, cinnamon and cloves rounding out the chili and shallot.
recipes.healthBenefit: Turmeric, galangal, lemongrass and raw aromatics bring flavour in small amounts, though the shrimp paste and fish sauce make the paste salty.

ingredients.prepNote: 2 1/2 tbsp fresh turmeric; in place of fresh turmeric root, which the database does not hold; fresh root counted as a quarter of its weight in ground turmeric
1 1/4 tbsp; in place of coriander root, which the database does not hold; leaves count for the root
the ground turmeric the source lists beside the fresh root
2 1/2 tsp at 4.2 g per tsp; in place of coconut sugar, which the database does not hold

instructions: Strip the centre ribs from the lime leaves and chop them fine. Grind the coriander seeds.
Pound the galangal and lemongrass in a mortar to a rough pulp and set it aside.
Pound the coriander root, chilies, fresh turmeric, shallots, garlic and lime leaves to a fine paste.
Return the galangal and lemongrass and pound until everything is fine.
Mix in the cumin, coriander seed, paprika, ground turmeric, cloves, cinnamon and chili powder.
Work in the fish sauce, shrimp paste, sugar and oil until smooth and golden. Keep refrigerated up to 1 week, or freeze in tablespoon portions for up to 3 months.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the fresh and ground turmeric.
From the shrimp paste and fish sauce.

recipes.name: Prik Gaeng Massaman (Massaman Curry Paste)

instructions: Toast the chilies, coriander seeds and cumin seeds in a dry pan over low heat until lightly browned and fragrant.
Grind them with the salt until very fine, then mix in the cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg and white pepper.
Chop the shallots, garlic, lemongrass, galangal, coriander root and lime peel finely.
Pound everything together to a smooth paste, then work in the shrimp paste. Keep refrigerated up to 1 week, or freeze in tablespoon portions for up to 3 months.

From the salt and shrimp paste.

recipes.name: Prik Gaeng Panang (Panang Curry Paste)
recipes.flavorProfile: Thick, hot and aromatic, a red paste of dried chilies and plenty of garlic with toasted coriander, cumin, mace and cardamom.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chilies, garlic, shallot and toasted spices bring a lot of flavour to a paste used in small amounts, though the salt and shrimp paste make it salty.

ingredients.cutPrep: seeded, the green ones browned first
ingredients.prepNote: about 16 red and 4 green long dried chilies
about 10 roots; in place of coriander root, which the database does not hold; leaves count for the root

instructions: Toast the coriander and cumin seeds in a dry pan over low heat until lightly browned, then brown the mace and cardamom in the same pan.
Brown the green chilies on both sides, then open all the chilies and remove the seeds.
Grind the chilies, mace, cardamom, cumin, coriander seed and peppercorns as fine as possible.
Grate the galangal and lime peel, slice the lemongrass and chop the coriander root, garlic and shallots, then pound them in a mortar until smooth.
Add the ground spices and salt and keep pounding until fine, then work in the shrimp paste. Freeze in 2 tablespoon portions and thaw only once.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the salt and shrimp paste.

recipes.name: Nam Prik Pao (Roasted Chili Jam)
recipes.flavorProfile: Sticky, sweet, smoky and gently hot, with roasted shallot and garlic and a savoury shrimp paste depth.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich condiment, high in sugar and oil, so it is a spoonful for flavour rather than a source of nutrients.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 cup; it stays in the jam
about 22 long and 45 small dried chilies
1 cup at 12.6 g per tbsp; in place of coconut sugar, which the database does not hold

instructions: Dry roast the chilies in a wok over medium high heat until they crackle and darken in spots, then set aside.
Roast the unpeeled shallots and garlic in the same pan until soft and charred in places. Cool, then peel.
Wrap the shrimp paste in foil and heat it in the pan until dry and crumbly.
Grind the chilies coarsely, seeds and all. Pound the shallots, garlic, shrimp paste and tamarind until smooth, then pound in the chilies and salt.
Fry the paste in the oil over low to medium heat, mashing it until it loosens, then about 5 minutes on low.
Add the fish sauce, water and sugar and simmer on low, stirring, until the sugar dissolves, then about 2 minutes more. Cool and keep in a jar in the refrigerator for up to 1 month.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the palm sugar, a large amount, so it is used by the spoonful.

recipes.name: Nam Soup Gai (Thai Chicken Stock)
recipes.flavorProfile: Clean and light, with coriander root, garlic and daikon, the base for clear soups and tom yum.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light stock that carries some protein and minerals from the bones and adds flavour with little fat once skimmed.

ingredients.baseName: Chicken, broiler, back, meat and skin
ingredients.prepNote: 1 chicken carcass or the same weight of backs, rinsed
3 coriander roots; the leaves row stands in, since the database holds no root

instructions: Bring the water to a boil in a large pot.
Add the chicken, daikon, coriander roots, onion, carrot, celery root, garlic and salt.
When it comes back to a gentle boil, turn the heat to low and skim off the foam.
Cover and simmer on low for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Strain through a fine sieve and discard the solids. Cool quickly, then refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. It makes about 8 cups.

instructions: Cover the tamarind with the water and leave it about 5 minutes without stirring, then squeeze and knead it with your fingers until the pulp comes away from the fibres.

recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, fragrant and slightly sticky, the plain rice that every central Thai meal is built around.
recipes.healthBenefit: A plain source of starch for energy, naturally gluten free and low in fat.
instructions: Rinse the rice in cold water 3 times, until the water runs nearly clear, and drain.
Bring the rice and water to a boil in a heavy pot, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 to 15 minutes.
Take off the heat and leave covered 10 minutes, then fluff with a paddle.

recipes.name: Khao Niao (Sticky Rice)

instructions: Soak the rice in plenty of cold water for at least 4 hours or overnight, then drain.

recipes.name: Kati (Fresh Coconut Milk)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fresh, sweet and creamy, lighter and cleaner tasting than canned coconut milk.
recipes.healthBenefit: Rich in saturated fat from the coconut, so it is a flavour base rather than a health food.

ingredients.prepNote: the squeezed pulp is discarded, so the nutrients here run higher than what is eaten

instructions: Knead the grated coconut with 300 ml of water for 2 to 3 minutes, then squeeze it hard through a cloth. This first press is the cream (hua kati).
Return the pulp to the bowl with the other 300 ml of water, knead and squeeze again for the thinner milk (hang kati).
Discard the pulp and keep the cream and milk refrigerated, separately if a recipe asks, for up to 2 days.

recipes.name: Moo Krob (Crispy Pork Belly)
recipes.flavorProfile: Shatteringly crisp crackling over juicy layered pork, salty and rich.
recipes.healthBenefit: High in protein and also in fat, a treat used in small amounts in stir fries.

ingredients.baseName: Gris sidfläsk bit rå m. svål

ingredients.prepNote: in the par-boiling water, which is poured away; the pork takes up only a little
in the par-boiling water, which is poured away
the share of frying oil the pork keeps

instructions: Cut the belly into strips about 4 cm thick and 15 cm long.
Bring enough water to cover the pork to a boil with the salt and vinegar, add the pork and simmer 5 to 10 minutes, just until the outside firms.
Drain and leave the pieces to dry thoroughly.
Fry in deep oil over medium heat about 10 minutes, partly covered as the oil spits, until the meat is golden. Lift out.
Heat the oil until it just begins to smoke and fry the pieces again about 1 minute, until the skin puffs and crackles.
Drain on a rack and cool before slicing. Keep refrigerated up to a week and slice only as needed.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork fat and skin.

recipes.name: Gaeng Kiew Wan Gai (Green Curry with Chicken)
recipes.flavorProfile: Creamy, hot and fragrant, with sweet basil, crunchy Thai eggplant and tender chicken in a pale green coconut sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken brings protein and the eggplants add fibre, while the coconut milk makes it a rich curry.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 cup; in place of pea eggplant (makhuea phuang), which the database does not hold
2 tbsp at 12.6 g per tbsp; in place of coconut sugar, which the database does not hold

ingredients.cutPrep: long red chili, sliced on the bias

instructions: Bring half the coconut milk to a bubble in a wok, add the curry paste and fry over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until the oil separates, without letting it brown.
Add the chicken, coat it, cover and cook 2 to 3 minutes a side.
Stir in the sugar until it dissolves and cook about 1 minute more.
Add the rest of the coconut milk, the green peppercorns and the whole lime leaves and bring to a boil.
Add both eggplants, cover and simmer about 5 minutes, until the Thai eggplants just soften, adding a little water if needed.
Off the heat, season with the fish sauce, stir in most of the basil and serve topped with the chili, the rest of the basil and the slivered lime leaves, with jasmine rice.

recipes.name: Gaeng Phed Ped Yang (Red Curry with Roast Duck)
recipes.flavorProfile: Rich and gently sweet, roast duck in a red coconut curry with bursts of juicy rambutan and cherry tomato.
recipes.healthBenefit: Duck gives protein and iron, though the duck skin and coconut milk make this a rich dish.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 1/2 tsp at 4.2 g per tsp; in place of palm sugar, which the database does not hold

instructions: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium low heat and fry the curry paste until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk, turn the heat to medium high and bring to a boil.
Add the stock, chilies, eggplants, tomatoes, rambutan and lime leaves, then turn the heat down to medium low.
Season with the palm sugar, salt and fish sauce.
Add the duck and bring back to a boil, stirring gently so the skin stays whole. Stir in the basil, take off the heat and serve with jasmine rice or thin rice noodles.

citations.source: Import Food, Roasted Duck Red Curry
Thai Cookbook TV, Red Curry with Bamboo Shoots

recipes.curationNote: Import Food, Roasted Duck Red Curry for every amount and step; serves 4, as ours.

recipes.name: Gaeng Massaman Neua (Massaman Beef Curry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Mellow, sweet, sour and warmly spiced, with beef braised until it falls apart, soft potatoes and roasted peanuts.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef gives protein, iron and zinc and the potatoes add potassium, though the coconut milk and sugar make it rich.

ingredients.prepNote: 3 tbsp at 12.6 g per tbsp; in place of palm sugar, which the database does not hold

instructions: Bring half the coconut milk to a boil in a pot over medium high heat and stir in the curry paste until smooth.
Lower the heat and add the beef, fish sauce, palm sugar, tamarind water, potatoes, peanuts, onion, half the tomatoes and the rest of the coconut milk.
Cover and simmer gently for about 1 hour, longer if the beef is not yet tender.
Stir in the rest of the tomatoes and serve with jasmine rice.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Massaman Beef Curry
Import Food, Massaman Beef

recipes.curationNote: Import Food, Massaman Beef for every amount and step; serves 4, as ours; the closest of the two cited, since it uses fish sauce as ours does.

recipes.name: Panang Neua (Panang Beef Curry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Thick, nutty and fragrant with shredded lime leaf, a dry curry that clings to thin slices of beef.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef gives protein and iron, with the coconut cream making it a rich dish.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 tbsp at 12.6 g per tbsp; in place of palm sugar, which the database does not hold

instructions: Heat half the coconut cream in a wok over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes, until the oil separates, then fry the paste 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the beef and stir 2 to 3 minutes, until no longer pink.
Add the coconut milk, fish sauce and palm sugar and simmer 3 to 5 minutes, until thick.
Stir in most of the lime leaf, then spoon over the remaining coconut cream and finish with chili, basil and the last lime leaf. Serve with jasmine rice.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Panang Beef Curry
Import Food, Thai Panang Pork

recipes.curationNote: Thai Cookbook TV, Panang Beef Curry for every amount and step; followed.

recipes.name: Gaeng Kari Gai (Yellow Chicken Curry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Mild, golden and comforting, chicken and soft potatoes in a turmeric coconut sauce, served with cool cucumber relish.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken brings protein and the potatoes potassium, with the coconut milk making it rich.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 tsp at 4.2 g per tsp; in place of palm sugar, which the database does not hold

instructions: Cook the chicken in the coconut milk in a pot over low heat until done.
In a wok, fry the curry paste until fragrant, then add the coconut cream a little at a time, stirring, until the oil rises.
Add the chicken, then tip everything back into the pot with the coconut milk.

Add the potatoes, bring to a boil, season with the fish sauce and palm sugar and simmer on low about 10 minutes, until the potatoes are soft. Top with fried shallots and serve with rice and the cucumber relish.

citations.source: Import Food, Thai Yellow Curry Chicken
Thai Cookbook TV, Chicken Yellow Curry

recipes.curationNote: Import Food, Thai Yellow Curry Chicken for every amount and step; serves 4, as ours.

recipes.name: Gaeng Som Goong (Sour Curry with Shrimp)
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin, sharp, hot and sour, a coconut free orange curry with shrimp and soft green papaya.
recipes.healthBenefit: Shrimp gives lean protein and the vegetables add fibre and vitamin A, with no coconut fat.

ingredients.prepNote: 0.5 tbsp at 12.6 g per tbsp; in place of palm sugar, which the database does not hold

instructions: Bring the water to a boil, stir in the curry paste and simmer 2 to 3 minutes.
Season with the tamarind water, fish sauce and palm sugar, aiming for sour first, then salty, then sweet.
Add the papaya, beans and carrot and simmer 5 to 7 minutes, until tender.
Add the shrimp and simmer 2 minutes, just until pink. Serve with jasmine rice.

citations.source: Hungry in Thailand, Kaeng Som
Wikipedia, Kaeng som

recipes.curationNote: Hungry in Thailand recipe followed for amounts and timing; Wikipedia for the central style with tamarind and no coconut.

recipes.name: Gaeng Pa (Jungle Curry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fierce, herbal and brothy, a coconut free curry of pork and crunchy vegetables with green peppercorn and holy basil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean pork and plenty of vegetables in a broth with no coconut, so it is lighter than most Thai curries.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 tbsp at 12.6 g per tbsp; in place of light brown sugar
in place of holy basil (kaphrao), which the database does not hold

instructions: Fry the paste in the oil in a wok over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the pork and stir 2 to 3 minutes, then the stock, fingerroot and green peppercorns, and bring to a simmer.
Add the eggplant, bamboo, beans and baby corn and simmer, covered, 8 to 10 minutes, until the vegetables are just tender.
Stir in the toasted rice, lime leaves, fish sauce and sugar, then the holy basil off the heat. Serve with jasmine rice.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the eggplant, beans, bamboo and baby corn.

citations.source: Tasting Table, Kaeng Pa With Fish
Wikipedia, Kaeng pa

recipes.curationNote: Tasting Table, Kaeng Pa With Fish for every amount and step; serves 6, as ours; made with pork in place of fish, with the fingerroot, green peppercorns and lime leaves Wikipedia names.

recipes.name: Gaeng Hang Lay Moo (Northern Pork Curry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Dark, sticky and sweet sour, pork belly and shoulder braised soft with ginger, pickled garlic and Burmese style spices.
recipes.healthBenefit: Protein from the pork with ginger and spices for flavour, though the belly and sugar make it a rich dish.

ingredients.baseName: Gris sidfläsk bit rå m. svål

ingredients.prepNote: part of 1/2 tbsp hang lay powder
part of 1/2 tbsp hang lay powder
part of 1/2 tbsp hang lay powder
part of 1/2 tbsp hang lay powder
part of 1/2 tbsp hang lay powder
part of 1/2 tbsp hang lay powder
3 tbsp at 12.6 g per tbsp; in place of palm sugar, which the database does not hold

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Mix the pork with the curry paste, spice powder and the brine from the pickled garlic and leave 1 hour, stirring halfway.
Stir fry the pork over medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes, until no longer pink.
Add the water, bring to a boil, then cook on low for 30 minutes, skimming off fat if you like.
Add the pickled garlic cloves, ginger and peanuts and cook over medium low for 30 minutes.
Add the dark soy, thin soy, palm sugar and tamarind and cook 30 minutes more, until sour, sweet and a little salty. Serve with sticky rice.

recipes.name: Choo Chee Pla (Choo Chee Fish Curry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp fried fish under a thick, sweet and savoury red coconut sauce scented with shredded lime leaf.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mackerel brings protein and omega 3 fats, while the frying and coconut milk make the dish rich.

ingredients.prepNote: the share of shallow frying oil the fish keeps

ingredients.cutPrep: a third of it cracked first

ingredients.prepNote: in place of palm sugar, which the database does not hold

instructions: Shallow fry the fish in oil at 350°F (175°C) for 3 to 4 minutes a side, until crisp and cooked through, and drain.
Heat a third of the coconut milk in a wok over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes, until the oil separates, then fry the paste 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the rest of the coconut milk, the fish sauce and palm sugar and simmer 5 to 8 minutes, until thick.
Pour the sauce over the fish and scatter with lime leaf and chili. Serve with jasmine rice.

Thai Cookbook TV, Red Curry with Bamboo Shoots

recipes.name: Gaeng Phed Fak Thong (Red Curry with Pumpkin)
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet, soft pumpkin and pork in a creamy red curry, mild heat with basil and lime leaf.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pumpkin brings vitamin A and fibre and the pork protein, with coconut milk making it rich.

ingredients.cutPrep: peeled and cut in 3 cm chunks

ingredients.prepNote: 1 tbsp at 12.6 g per tbsp; in place of palm sugar, which the database does not hold

instructions: Heat the coconut cream in a wok over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring, until it bubbles and the oil separates (cracks). Fry the paste 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the pork and stir 3 to 4 minutes, until cooked on the outside.
Add the coconut milk, water and pumpkin and simmer 8 to 12 minutes, until the pumpkin is tender but holds its shape.
Add the lime leaves, fish sauce and palm sugar, then the basil and chili off the heat. Serve with jasmine rice.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Yellow Curry with Pumpkin and Pork
Thai Cookbook TV, Red Curry with Bamboo Shoots

recipes.name: Gaeng Tai Pla (Southern Fish Organ Curry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Intensely savoury, pungent and hot, a turmeric yellow broth of fermented fish innards with dried fish and vegetables.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fish and vegetables in a broth with no coconut milk, though the tai pla makes it very salty.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, rice, white, long-grain, regular, dry

ingredients.prepNote: in place of fresh turmeric root, which the database does not hold; the source names turmeric without an amount

ingredients.name: tai pla (fermented fish innards)
ingredients.prepNote: bought in a jar, never made at home; boiled in the water and strained, so only the liquid stays
1 whole dried fish, about 80 g; unsalted dried cod stands in for the Thai dried fish
the source names green beans without an amount

instructions: Soak the dried chilies until soft and squeeze them dry. Pound them with the salt, raw rice, peppercorns, lemongrass, garlic, lime peel and turmeric, then the shrimp paste, into a smooth paste.
Bring the water to a boil, add the tai pla and boil 5 minutes, then strain out the solids and return the liquid to the pot.
Stir in the paste, bring back to a boil, and add the dried fish, bamboo shoot, eggplants and beans. Simmer until the vegetables are tender, about 10 minutes.
Season with the sugar and lime juice and tear in the lime leaves. Taste before adding any salt, since tai pla is very salty. Serve with jasmine rice.

nutritionHighlights.note: Very high, from the fermented fish and shrimp paste.

citations.source: Import Food, Gaeng Tai Pla
Wikipedia, Kaeng tai pla

recipes.curationNote: Import Food's recipe from a Trang cook, serves 4, amounts kept. Tai pla is bought jarred. The dried fish weight is an estimate for one whole fish.

recipes.name: Tom Yum Goong (Hot and Sour Shrimp Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: Hot, sour and fragrant, a clear lemongrass and galangal broth with sweet shrimp and a slick of roasted chili jam.
recipes.healthBenefit: Shrimp gives lean protein in a broth with almost no fat, though the fish sauce makes it salty.

ingredients.cutPrep: 3 stalks, cut in 4 cm lengths and bruised
peeled and deveined, heads kept for the broth if you have them
ingredients.prepNote: 8 large shrimp at about 25 g each

instructions: Bring the stock to a boil with the lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and simmer 2 minutes, then the shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes, just until pink.
Turn off the heat and stir in the fish sauce, chili jam and chilies.
Add the lime juice off the heat, so it stays fresh, top with cilantro and serve with jasmine rice.

citations.source: Import Food, Tom Yum Goong
Thai Cookbook TV, Tom Yum Goong

recipes.curationNote: Import Food, Tom Yum Goong for every amount and step; serves 4 with 4 cups stock, as ours.

recipes.name: Tom Kha Gai (Coconut Chicken Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: Creamy, tangy and gently hot, with the peppery perfume of galangal running through a coconut broth.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken and mushrooms bring protein and B vitamins, with coconut milk making it a rich soup.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 stalk, lower part only, bruised and cut in lengths

ingredients.baseName: Chicken, broiler, thigh, meat without skin

ingredients.prepNote: half added with the coconut milk, the rest to taste
shaved (1 tsp; in place of palm sugar, which the database does not hold)
2 Thai chilies, lightly crushed (the source says 1 to 3)
chopped, to serve (the source gives no amount)

instructions: Bring the chicken stock to a boil, add the salt and the chicken, lower the heat and simmer gently about 15 minutes, until the chicken is tender and reaches 165°F (74°C).
Add the coconut milk, lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, chilies, mushrooms, the sugar and about half the fish sauce, and stir gently.
Keep it at a gentle simmer, never a hard boil, for about 5 minutes so the aromatics flavor the broth and the mushrooms cook.
Taste, add the rest of the fish sauce only if it needs it, and turn off the heat.
Off the heat, stir in the lime juice, tasting as you go. Scatter the cilantro over and serve with jasmine rice. The lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves are not eaten.

citations.source: Portail Asie, Tom Kha Gai

recipes.curationNote: Portail Asie, Tom Kha Gai for every amount and step; serves 4, the same as ours: 500 ml unsalted chicken stock, 400 ml coconut milk, 1/2 tsp salt, 450 g skinless chicken thigh, 1 lemongrass stalk, 12 thin galangal slices, 5 makrut lime leaves, 1 to 3 Thai chilies, 160 g oyster mushrooms, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp palm sugar, 2 1/2 tbsp lime juice, cilantro or scallions to serve. The Nam Soup Gai component (2 cups) stands for the 500 ml stock, made without salt.

recipes.name: Tom Saep (Isan Hot and Sour Pork Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fiery, sour and herbal, a clear pork rib broth with toasted rice, roasted chili and culantro.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork ribs give protein in a broth with no coconut, though the ribs carry fat and the fish sauce salt.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Blanch the ribs in boiling water for 5 minutes, drain and rinse.
Cover with the fresh water, add the lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves and shallots and simmer gently for 60 to 75 minutes, until the meat is tender.
Season with the fish sauce and simmer 5 minutes more.
Off the heat, stir in the lime juice, chilies, chili flakes and toasted rice, then the herbs. Serve with sticky rice.

citations.source: Portail Asie, Tom Saap
Import Food, Tom Yum Goong

recipes.curationNote: Portail Asie is the one tom saep recipe that opened and is followed closely; Import Food only for the shared lime off the heat method.

recipes.name: Gaeng Jued Tao Hoo (Clear Soup with Tofu)
recipes.flavorProfile: Mild, clean and peppery, a gentle broth with soft tofu, pork meatballs and sweet cabbage.
recipes.healthBenefit: Tofu and pork give protein in a light, low fat broth, an easy soup for an unsettled day.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.prepNote: 1 tbsp at 5 g per tbsp; in place of coriander root, which the database does not hold; leaves count for the root

instructions: Mix the pork with the soy sauce, ground black pepper and salt.
Pound the garlic, shallots, coriander root and peppercorns together and simmer them in the stock for 5 minutes.
Drop in the pork in small balls and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, then add the cabbage for 3 minutes.
Slide in the tofu, season with the fish sauce and simmer 2 minutes more. Top with cilantro and fried shallots and serve with rice.

recipes.name: Tom Kha Hed (Coconut Mushroom Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: Silky, sour and fragrant, three kinds of mushroom in a galangal coconut broth.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mushrooms bring B vitamins and fibre, and this version is meat free, though the coconut milk makes it rich.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 stalk, lower part only, bruised and cut in lengths

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
ingredients.prepNote: in place of the fish sauce, one for one; half with the coconut milk, the rest to taste
shaved (1 tsp; in place of palm sugar, which the database does not hold)
2 Thai chilies, lightly crushed (the source says 1 to 3)
chopped, to serve (the source gives no amount)

instructions: Bring the vegetable stock to a boil with the salt, then lower to a gentle simmer.
Add the coconut milk, lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, chilies, all the mushrooms, the sugar and about half the soy sauce, and stir gently.
Keep it at a gentle simmer, never a hard boil, for about 5 minutes, until the mushrooms are tender.
Taste, add the rest of the soy sauce only if it needs it, and turn off the heat.
Off the heat, stir in the lime juice, tasting as you go. Scatter the cilantro over and serve with jasmine rice. The lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves are not eaten.

recipes.name: Poh Taek (Seafood Hot and Sour Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: Hot, sour and herbal, a clear tom yum style broth crowded with shrimp, squid, mussels and fish, with sweet basil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mixed seafood gives lean protein, iron and selenium in a broth with almost no fat, though salty.

ingredients.prepNote: 2 stalks, cut in 1 1/2 to 2 inch lengths

ingredients.cutPrep: in the shell, cleaned (weight of meat)

ingredients.prepNote: peeled and deveined, tails left on
6 green and red bird's eye chilies
1 cup sweet basil leaves, the leaf the source names
2 dried red chilies, lightly fried and cut in 1/2 inch pieces, to garnish

instructions: Bring the stock to a boil over medium heat with the salt. Add the lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves and cook until fragrant.
Add the fish, squid and mussels without stirring and cook until they change colour, then add the shrimp. Discard any mussels that stay shut.
Cook a few minutes more, until the shrimp turn pink, add the basil, swirl gently and turn off the heat.
Meanwhile, mix the lime juice, fresh chilies and fish sauce in a serving bowl.
Pour the seafood and broth into the serving bowl, mix from the bottom up, and scatter the fried dried chilies over. Serve with jasmine rice.

citations.source: Family Cookbook Project, Thai Spicy Seafood (Po Taek) Soup

recipes.curationNote: Family Cookbook Project, Thai Spicy Seafood (Po Taek) Soup for every amount and step; the page cites all-thailand-exp.com, which no longer opens. It uses 2 cups water or chicken stock, 50 g each of shrimp, sea bass, squid, mussels and crab (the last two optional), 5 lime leaves, 3 galangal slices, 1 lemongrass stalk, 2 1/2 tbsp fish sauce, 2 1/2 tbsp lime juice, 1/2 cup sweet basil, a pinch of salt, 3 bird's eye chilies and 1 fried dried chili. It gives no serving count and some fractions are garbled on the page; ours uses 4 cups of stock, so every amount is doubled.

recipes.name: Khao Tom (Rice Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soothing and savoury, soft rice grains in a light pork broth with ginger, garlic oil and fried shallots.
recipes.healthBenefit: A gentle, easy to eat soup of rice and a little pork, light on fat apart from the garlic oil.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

ingredients.prepNote: about half of 7 to 8 shallots; the rest are the fried shallots

ingredients.cutPrep: cut in pieces, lifted out before serving

ingredients.baseName: Pepper, hot chili, red or green

instructions: Warm the oil in the soup pot and briefly fry the garlic and chopped shallots, then cook the pork until no pink remains.
Add the water and bring it to a boil, then add the lemongrass and most of the ginger and boil hard about 5 minutes.
Lift out the lemongrass, add the rice and stir in the green onion, cilantro, fish sauce and lime juice. Boil about 1 minute and turn off the heat.
Taste and adjust with fish sauce or lime, then serve topped with the fried shallots, the rest of the ginger, more green onion and cilantro, and the chili.

recipes.name: Pad Kra Pao (Holy Basil Stir-Fry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Hot, salty and peppery with the clove like bite of holy basil, served over rice with a crisp edged fried egg.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork and egg give protein, though the dish is salty and the egg is fried.

ingredients.cutPrep: bird chilies, pounded with the garlic

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.prepNote: in place of holy basil (kaphrao), which the database does not hold
the share of egg frying oil the eggs keep

instructions: Fry the eggs in hot oil, about 375°F (190°C), spooning oil over them for 1 to 2 minutes until the edges are crisp and the yolk soft. Set aside.
Heat a wok over high heat until it smokes lightly, about 400°F (205°C) at the surface, then add the oil. Fry the garlic and chilies 10 to 15 seconds.
Add the pork and stir-fry 2 to 3 minutes, breaking it up, until cooked through.
Add the sauces, sugar and water and toss 30 seconds, then the holy basil until just wilted. Serve over rice with the egg on top.

Import Food, Gai Pad Krapao

recipes.name: Pad Pak Ruam (Mixed Vegetable Stir-Fry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp, glossy and savoury, a garlicky toss of colourful vegetables in oyster sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: A plate of many vegetables, bringing fibre, vitamin A, vitamin C and folate.
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat and fry the garlic until fragrant without letting it brown.
Raise the heat, add the carrot and cauliflower and stir-fry a minute, then add the corn, snow peas, mushrooms and the bok choy stems and stir-fry until they start to soften.
Add the bok choy leaves, the oyster sauce and the stock, stir, cover and cook 1 minute.
Uncover, sprinkle with the sesame oil and white pepper and serve with the rice.

From the cauliflower, snow peas and bok choy.

recipes.name: Gai Pad Med Mamuang (Cashew Chicken)
recipes.flavorProfile: Savoury, slightly sweet and smoky, golden chicken with toasted cashews and crisp fried dried chilies.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken brings protein and the cashews magnesium and unsaturated fat, with frying making it richer.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.prepNote: the share of frying oil the dish keeps

ingredients.cutPrep: long dried chilies, cut in 2 cm pieces

ingredients.prepNote: in place of 1 or 2 wax peppers, which the database does not hold

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Stir the white pepper into the flour and toss the chicken in it until lightly coated.
Heat the oil until just warm and fry the cashews over low heat about 5 minutes, until lightly browned, then drain. Fry the dried chilies a few seconds until they brighten and drain.
Fry the chicken on low heat about 5 minutes, until cooked through (165°F, 74°C), and drain.
Pour off all but about 1 tablespoon of oil, fry the garlic 30 seconds, then the onion 1 minute.
Add the oyster sauce, both soy sauces and the sugar with a little of the water to make a thick sauce, then the chicken and the rest of the water over high heat for 1 minute.
Add the cashews for 2 minutes, then the fresh chilies, peppers and green onions for 30 seconds. Top with the fried dried chilies and serve with rice.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Cashew Chicken
Import Food, Thai Cashew Chicken

recipes.name: Pad Pak Boong (Stir-Fried Morning Glory)
recipes.flavorProfile: Smoky, salty and garlicky, tender hollow stems flashed in a roaring wok with fermented soybean.
recipes.healthBenefit: Morning glory brings vitamin A, vitamin C and iron, though the sauces add salt.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 tbsp at 18 g per tbsp; in place of fermented yellow soybean paste (tao jiao), which the database does not hold

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Put the morning glory, garlic, chilies, soybean paste, sauces, sugar and water together in a bowl.
Heat a wok over high heat until it smokes lightly, about 400°F (205°C) at the surface, then add the oil. Tip in everything at once; it will flare.
Toss over high heat for 45 to 60 seconds, just until the leaves wilt and the stems stay crisp. Serve at once with rice.

recipes.name: Pad Cha Talay (Spicy Seafood Stir-Fry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Wild, herbal and hot, mixed seafood tossed with fingerroot, fresh green peppercorns and lime leaf.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mixed seafood gives lean protein, iron and selenium, with salt from the sauces.

ingredients.cutPrep: yellow spur chilies, for the paste
red spur chilies, sliced on the bias

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.prepNote: in place of holy basil (kaphrao), which the database does not hold

ingredients.name: fresh green peppercorns
ingredients.prepNote: 4 to 5 strands at about 3 g each; neither database holds fresh green peppercorns

instructions: Pound the shallot, garlic, chilies, white pepper and fingerroot for the paste into a coarse paste, 5 to 8 minutes.
Heat a wok over high heat until it smokes lightly, about 400°F (205°C) at the surface, then add the oil. Fry the paste 30 to 60 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the eggplant and stir-fry 1 minute, then all the seafood with the sauces, sugar and stock and toss 2 to 3 minutes, until just cooked.
Add the fingerroot, green peppercorns, spur chilies, lime leaves and basil and toss 30 seconds. Serve with rice.

recipes.name: Gai Pad Khing (Ginger Chicken)
recipes.flavorProfile: Warm, savoury and lightly sweet, chicken with lots of fresh ginger, green onion and crunchy cloud ear.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean chicken breast gives protein, with salt from the oyster and soy sauces.

ingredients.baseName: Mushrooms, tree ears, Cloud ear fungus, dried
ingredients.cutPrep: dried weight, soaked 20 to 30 minutes and sliced

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)
ingredients.cutPrep: half cut in 2 cm lengths, half left whole

instructions: Soak the cloud ear in warm water for 20 to 30 minutes, trim off the hard base and tear it into pieces. Have everything measured before you start.
Warm the oil in a wok over low heat and fry the garlic gently for about 30 seconds.
Turn the heat to medium high, add the chicken and keep it moving for about 2 minutes.
Add the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar and black pepper, then the water, and cook about 2 minutes until the sauce thickens and the chicken is cooked (165°F, 74°C).
Stir in the cloud ear for about 2 minutes, then the ginger, cut green onions and chilies for about 1 minute.
Serve at once with rice, with the whole green onions alongside.

recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp, slightly bitter greens and crackling pork belly tossed with garlic, chili and oyster sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chinese broccoli brings vitamin C, vitamin K and calcium, with the crispy pork making it rich.

instructions: Heat a wok over high heat until it smokes lightly, about 400°F (205°C) at the surface, then add the oil. Fry the garlic and chilies 10 to 15 seconds.

recipes.name: Pad Prik Gaeng Moo (Pork Stir-Fried with Curry Paste)
recipes.flavorProfile: Dry, hot and fragrant, crispy pork belly fried in red curry paste with long beans and lime leaf.
recipes.healthBenefit: Long beans add fibre beside the protein of the pork, though the crispy belly makes this a treat.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 tsp at 4.2 g per tsp; in place of palm sugar, which the database does not hold

instructions: Fry the curry paste in the oil in a wok over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until fragrant and dark.
Add the long beans and water and stir-fry 1 to 2 minutes, until bright green.
Add the palm sugar, fish sauce and crispy pork and toss 30 to 60 seconds, then the lime leaf and basil. Serve with rice.
